content: {"summary":"During the 03:00‑06:35 UTC window on 23 July 2026 both notification‑worker pods experienced DNS lookup latency that manifested as 5‑second stalls and occasional EAI_AGAIN errors.","likely_cause":"ndots:5 caused each lookup to generate multiple UDP queries; occasional lost replies triggered the resolver’s 5 s timeout and retries, and the 4‑thread libuv pool amplified the impact during traffic bursts.","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"Both pods show slow lookups and EAI_AGAIN in their logs","evidence_ids":["INC-0179#0"],"quote":"Both pods show slow lookups and `EAI_AGAIN` in their logs."},{"text":"ndots:5 expands short names, creating many queries per lookup","evidence_ids":["RB-021#4"],"quote":"ndots:5 means a name with fewer than five dots gets each search suffix appended first"},{"text":"Lost UDP replies cause the resolver to wait 5 s before retrying","evidence_ids":["RB-021#4"],"quote":"When a reply is missing, the resolver waits out its 5 s timeout and asks that query again;"},{"text":"Two lost replies recovered by retry add about 10 s latency","evidence_ids":["RB-021#5"],"quote":"Two lost replies each recovered by its retry, cost about 10 s"},{"text":"The libuv thread pool has only four threads, so a hanging lookup blocks a thread and queues other work","evidence_ids":["RB-021#1"],"quote":"While a lookup hangs, it keeps one of them busy."}],"next_checks":["Check whether the notification‑worker Deployment overrides ndots to reduce query count","Inspect cluster DNS server logs for UDP packet loss during the incident window","Monitor libuv thread‑pool utilization in notification‑worker pods under load","Measure DNS query success rate and latency for the affected record"]}
